Sean Esbjorn-Hargens is a scholar of consciousness who has studied experiencers, people who report alien encounters, and the brain scans some researchers have taken of them. With Danny Jones, he discusses what those scans appear to show and his claim that they reveal a gateway to a hidden world ordinary perception misses.

Esbjorn-Hargens works where neuroscience, philosophy, and the encounter literature meet, and he tries to give each its due. Jones asks what a scan can and cannot prove about an experience. The findings discussed are preliminary and disputed, and the episode presents them as the guest's reading. Listeners get a credentialed attempt to take experiencers seriously as data rather than as jokes or prophets, which is this guest's whole project, preserved in his own measured words.

Andrew Huberman explains, in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience, why scientists kept company with Jeffrey Epstein. The financier courted researchers with money and access before his crimes became front-page news. Huberman, a working scientist, gives an insider's view of that world.

He describes how labs chase funding, how a rich patron opens doors, and why smart people missed or ignored the warning signs. Rogan asks whether the money warped the science it bought. The segment is a frank look at the funding web behind elite research, from a man who has had to raise money inside it.
